headline: Commission on Persons with Disabilities

meeting.summary: Six commissioners were present, enough to hold the meeting.
meeting.recap: Six commissioners were present, enough to hold the meeting.[[0:02:20]] A testifier asked for short, paved paths so wheelchair users can reach scenic overlooks.[[0:06:35]] Another testifier asked the commission to request the checklist the Planning Department uses to review special management area permits.[[0:15:03]] The commission approved the minutes of its July 9, 2026 meeting.[[0:21:38]] A commissioner volunteered to work on a way to track public accessibility complaints and report back.[[0:39:23]] A commissioner described harsh treatment by police during an arrest and asked that someone who understands disability sit on the police commission.[[0:44:50]] The commission voted on a motion to send two letters to the mayor.[[1:00:28]] A proposed housing project has 22 homes: seven for adults with disabilities and 17 affordable rentals open to anyone.[[1:34:29]] Aging office staff said a man in FEMA housing in Kīhei who became disabled was told to move back to Lahaina, away from his services.[[1:48:38]]
decided: The commission approved the July 9, 2026 regular meeting minutes.
The commission took a voice vote on sending two letters to the mayor, but no result was announced.
The chair kept the proposed housing project on the agenda for more discussion without a motion.
A motion to adjourn was made and seconded.
meeting.next: Fair organizers will meet next week with a couple who may chair Special Fair Day. The trail-access topic from public testimony could be placed on the next meeting's agenda.
